title.raw: 卷十四 本紀第十四: 順宗 憲宗上 Volume 14 Annals 14: Shunzong, Xianzong 1

sentences.zh: 順宗順宗至德大聖大安孝皇帝諱誦，德宗長子，母昭德皇后王氏。

translations.literal: Shunzong — Emperor Shunzong, posthumous title To the Utmost Virtue Great Sage Great Peace Filial, taboo name Song, eldest son of Dezong; mother Empress Zhaode, née Wang.
translations.idiomatic: Shunzong, the Filial Emperor Song, was Dezong's eldest son; his mother was Empress Zhaode Wang.

sentences.zh: 上元二年正月生於長安之東內。

translations.literal: In the first month of Shangyuan 2 he was born in the Eastern Inner Palace at Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was born in the eastern palace quarter of Chang'an in Shangyuan 2.

sentences.zh: 大曆十四年六月，封宣王。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of Dali 14 he was enfeoffed Prince of Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: In Dali 14 he received the title Prince of Xuan.

sentences.zh: 建中元年正月丁卯，立為皇太子。

translations.literal: In the first month of Jianzhong 1, on dingmao, he was installed as heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He became crown prince on dingmao in the first month of Jianzhong 1.

sentences.zh: 貞元二十一年正月癸巳，德宗崩，丙申，即位於太極殿。

translations.literal: In the first month of Zhenyuan 21, on guisi, Dezong died; on bingshen he took the throne in the Hall of Supreme Ultimate.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong died on guisi; three days later Shunzong ascended at the Hall of Supreme Ultimate.

sentences.zh: 上自二十年九月風病，不能言，暨德宗不豫，諸王親戚皆侍醫藥，獨上臥病不能侍。

translations.literal: The Emperor from the ninth month of year 20 had wind illness and could not speak; when Dezong fell gravely ill, all princes and kin attended with medicine — only the Emperor lay ill and could not attend.
translations.idiomatic: Since Zhenyuan 20 he had been speechless from a stroke; when Dezong lay dying, he alone could not attend the sickbed.

sentences.zh: 德宗彌留，思見太子，涕咽久之。

translations.literal: As Dezong lingered, he longed to see the heir; he wept and choked for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed Dezong wept to see the crown prince he could not summon.

sentences.zh: 大行發喪，人情震懼。

translations.literal: When the late Emperor's mourning began, people's hearts were shaken with fear.
translations.idiomatic: The court trembled when the imperial mourning was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 上力疾衰服，見百僚於九仙門。

translations.literal: The Emperor, forcing himself despite illness, wore mourning garments and received the hundred officials at the Nine Immortals Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He dragged himself into mourning dress to receive officials at the Nine Immortals Gate.

sentences.zh: 既即位，知社稷有奉，中外始安。

translations.literal: Once enthroned, knowing the altars had a bearer, within and without began to be at peace.
translations.idiomatic: His accession assured the realm that the throne was filled, and fear eased.

sentences.zh: 庚子，群臣上書請聽政。

translations.literal: On gengzi the host of ministers submitted memorials asking that he hear government.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi the bureaucracy petitioned him to take up rule.

sentences.zh: 二月辛丑朔。

translations.literal: Second month, xinchou new moon.
translations.idiomatic: The second month opened on xinchou.

sentences.zh: 甲申，以河陽三城行軍司馬元韶為懷州刺史、河陽懷州節度使。

translations.literal: On jiashen Yuan Shao, staff officer of the Three Cities of Heyang campaign army, was made prefect of Huai and commissioner of Heyang-Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao became Heyang-Huai commissioner on jiashen.

sentences.zh: 丙午，罷翰林醫工、相工、占星、射覆、冗食者四十二人。

translations.literal: On bingwu forty-two supernumeraries were dismissed — Hanlin medical artisans, physiognomists, astrologers, diviners by casting, and idle eaters.
translations.idiomatic: Forty-two court fortune-tellers and hangers-on were cut on bingwu.

sentences.zh: 己酉，以易定張茂昭兼同平章事，以來朝，故寵之。

translations.literal: On jiyou Zhang Maozhao of Yiding was made concurrent Grand Councillor, favored because he had come to court.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Maozhao received a concurrent premiership as reward for his visit.

sentences.zh: 是夜，太白犯昴。

translations.literal: That night Venus trespassed upon the Pleiades.
translations.idiomatic: Venus crossed the Pleiades that night.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，以吏部郎中韋執誼為尚書左丞、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: On xinmao Wei Zhiyi, bureau director in the Ministry of Personnel, was made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhiyi entered the council on xinmao.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，貶京兆尹李實通州長史，尋卒。

translations.literal: On xinyou Metropolitan Governor Li Shi was demoted to long-term administrator of Tongzhou; he soon died.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi, exiled to Tongzhou, died shortly after on xinyou.

sentences.zh: 壬子，淄青李師古以兵寇滑之東鄙，聞國喪也。

translations.literal: On renzi Li Shigu of Ziqing raided the eastern marches of Hua with troops, having heard of the national mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shigu attacked Hua's border on renzi, exploiting the mourning.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，釋仗內囚嚴懷志、呂溫等一十六人。

translations.literal: On jiayin sixteen prisoners of the inner guard — Yan Huaizhi, Lü Wen, and others — were released.
translations.idiomatic: Sixteen men long held in the inner guard were freed on jiayin.

sentences.zh: 平涼之盟陷蕃。

translations.literal: At the Pingliang pact they had fallen into Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: They had been captured when the Pingliang treaty party was seized by Tibet.

sentences.zh: 久之得還，以習蕃中事，不欲令出外，故囚之仗內，至是方釋之。

translations.literal: After long years they returned; because they knew Tibetan affairs, they were not wished outside — hence imprisoned in the inner guard; only now were they released.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Tibetan secrets, they had been kept in the palace guard until this release.

sentences.zh: 日本國王並妻還蕃，賜物遣之。

translations.literal: The king of Japan and his wife also returned to Tibet; gifts were bestowed and they were sent off.
translations.idiomatic: A Japanese king and queen were likewise sent home to Tibet with gifts.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，以太子侍書、翰林待詔王伾為左散騎常侍，充翰林學士。

translations.literal: On renyin Wang Pi, attendant calligrapher to the heir, and Hanlin awaiting-edict, was made Left Regular Cavalry Attendant and Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pi joined the Hanlin on renyin.

sentences.zh: 以前司功參軍、翰林待詔王叔文為起居舍人，充翰林學士。

translations.literal: Former staff officer in the Ministry of Justice, Hanlin awaiting-edict Wang Shuwen was made Diary Attendant and Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shuwen entered the Hanlin as diary attendant.

sentences.zh: 以鴻臚卿王權為京兆尹。

translations.literal: Minister of Diplomatic Reception Wang Quan was made Metropolitan Governor.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Quan became capital intendant.

sentences.zh: 甲子，禦丹鳳樓，大赦天下。

translations.literal: On jiazi he took Danfeng Tower and proclaimed a great amnesty for the empire.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty was proclaimed from Danfeng Tower on jiazi.

sentences.zh: 諸道除正敕率稅外，諸色榷稅並宜禁斷；

translations.literal: In all circuits, apart from regular statutory tax rates in imperial orders, every sort of monopoly levy should be forbidden;
translations.idiomatic: The edict banned circuit monopoly taxes beyond the statutory rates;

sentences.zh: 除上供外，不得別有進奉。

translations.literal: apart from tribute to the court, there must be no separate presentations.
translations.idiomatic: and barred extra tribute presentations.

sentences.zh: 百姓九十已上，賜米二石，絹兩匹，版授上佐、縣君，仍令本部長吏就家存問；

translations.literal: Commoners ninety and above were granted two piculs of grain and two bolts of silk, given honorary posts as Senior Assistant and District Lady, and their circuit magistrates were ordered to visit them at home;
translations.idiomatic: Nonagenarians received grain, silk, and honorary titles, with local officials sent to inquire after them;

sentences.zh: 百歲已上，賜米五石，絹二匹，綿一屯，羊酒，版授下州刺史、郡君。

translations.literal: those one hundred and above were granted five piculs of grain, two bolts of silk, one bundle of cotton, sheep and wine, and honorary posts as Lower Prefect and Commandery Lady.
translations.idiomatic: centenarians received richer gifts and higher honorary ranks.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，以開府儀同三司、檢校太尉、使持節、大都督雞林州諸軍事、雞林州刺史、上柱國、新羅王金重熙兼甯海軍使，以重熙母和氏為太妃，妻朴氏為妃。

translations.literal: On wuchen Kim Chung-hee of Silla, Grand Mentor of the Palace, acting Grand General, military commissioner of Gyerim, and pillar of the state, was also made commissioner of the Ninghai army; his mother Lady He was made Grand Consort, his wife Lady Pak consort.
translations.idiomatic: The Silla king received added titles and his kin were ennobled on wuchen.

sentences.zh: 三月庚午，出宮女三百人于安國寺，又出掖庭教坊女樂六百人於九仙門，召其親族歸之。

translations.literal: Third month, gengwu — three hundred palace women were sent out to Anguo Temple; six hundred women musicians of the inner palace and teaching workshops were sent out at the Nine Immortals Gate and their kin summoned to take them home.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month hundreds of palace women and musicians were released to their families.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，以韋皋兼檢校太尉，李師古、劉濟兼檢校司空。

translations.literal: On wuyin Wei Gao was made acting Grand General; Li Shigu and Liu Ji were made acting Masters of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Gao and two warlords received honorary grand titles on wuyin.

sentences.zh: 張茂昭司徒。

translations.literal: Zhang Maozhao was made Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Maozhao became Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，檢校司空、同平章事杜祐為度支鹽鐵使。

translations.literal: On bingxu Du You, acting Master of Works and Grand Councillor, was made commissioner of revenue, salt, and iron.
translations.idiomatic: Du You took the fiscal commission on bingxu.

sentences.zh: 戊子，徐州節度賜名武寧軍。

translations.literal: On wuzi the Xuzhou command was given the name Wuning Army.
translations.idiomatic: Xuzhou's army was renamed Wuning on wuzi.

sentences.zh: 蔡州吳少誠兼同平章事。

translations.literal: Wu Shao-cheng of Cai was made concurrent Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shao-cheng of Cai received a concurrent premiership.

sentences.zh: 以翰林學士王叔文為度支鹽鐵轉運副使。

translations.literal: Hanlin academician Wang Shuwen was made vice commissioner of revenue, salt, iron, and transport.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shuwen took the transport vice-commission.

sentences.zh: 杜祐雖領使名，其實叔文專總。

translations.literal: Although Du You bore the commissioner's title, in fact Shuwen held overall control.
translations.idiomatic: Du You was nominal head; Wang Shuwen ran fiscal policy.

sentences.zh: 宰相賈耽兼檢校司空，鄭瑜吏部尚書，高郢刑部尚書，韋執誼中書侍郎，鎮冀王士真、淮南王鍔、魏博田季安皆檢校司空。

translations.literal: Grand Councillor Jia Dan was made acting Master of Works; Zheng Yu Minister of Personnel; Gao Ying Minister of Justice; Wei Zhiyi Vice Director of the Secretariat; Wang Shizhen of Zhenji, Wang E of Huainan, and Tian Ji'an of Weibo were all made acting Masters of Works.
translations.idiomatic: A round of ministerial and honorary appointments followed for court and frontier leaders.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，詔冊廣陵郡王淳為皇太子，改名純。

translations.literal: On guisi an edict enfeoffed Prince of Guangling Chun as heir apparent; his name was changed to Chun.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Chun of Guangling became heir apparent as Chun on guisi.

sentences.zh: 夏四月壬寅，制第十弟諤封欽王，第十一弟諴封珍王。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, renyin — an order enfeoffed the tenth younger brother E as Prince of Qin and the eleventh Yan as Prince of Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Two imperial brothers were enfeoffed in the fourth month.

sentences.zh: 男建康郡王渙封郯王，改名經；

translations.literal: The son, Prince of Jiankang Huan, was enfeoffed Prince of Tan; his name was changed to Jing;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Huan of Jiankang became Prince of Tan as Jing;

sentences.zh: 洋川郡王沔封均王，改名緯；

translations.literal: Prince of Yangchuan Mian, Prince of Jun; his name was changed to Wei;
translations.idiomatic: Mian of Yangchuan became Prince of Jun as Wei;

sentences.zh: 臨淮郡王洵封漵王，改名縱；

translations.literal: Prince of Linhuai Xun, Prince of Yi; his name was changed to Zong;
translations.idiomatic: Xun of Linhuai became Prince of Yi as Zong;

sentences.zh: 弘農王浼封莒王，改名紓；

translations.literal: Prince of Hongnong Mei, Prince of Ju; his name was changed to Shu;
translations.idiomatic: Mei of Hongnong became Prince of Ju as Shu;

sentences.zh: 漢東郡王泳封密王，改名綢；

translations.literal: Prince of Handong Yong, Prince of Mi; his name was changed to Chou;
translations.idiomatic: Yong of Handong became Prince of Mi as Chou;

sentences.zh: 晉陵郡王堤封郇王，改名總；

translations.literal: Prince of Jinling Di, Prince of Xun; his name was changed to Zong;
translations.idiomatic: Di of Jinling became Prince of Xun as Zong;

sentences.zh: 高平郡王漵封邵王，改名約；

translations.literal: Prince of Gaoping Su, Prince of Shao; his name was changed to Yue;
translations.idiomatic: Su of Gaoping became Prince of Shao as Yue;

sentences.zh: 雲安郡王滋封宋王，改名結；

translations.literal: Prince of Yun'an Zi, Prince of Song; his name was changed to Jie;
translations.idiomatic: Zi of Yun'an became Prince of Song as Jie;

sentences.zh: 宣城郡王淮封集王，改名緗；

translations.literal: Prince of Xuancheng Huai, Prince of Ji; his name was changed to Xiang;
translations.idiomatic: Huai of Xuancheng became Prince of Ji as Xiang;

sentences.zh: 德陽郡王湑封冀王，改名絿；

translations.literal: Prince of Deyang Xu, Prince of Ji; his name was changed to Gui;
translations.idiomatic: Xu of Deyang became Prince of Ji as Gui;

sentences.zh: 河東郡王浥封和王，改名綺。

translations.literal: Prince of Hedong Yi, Prince of He; his name was changed to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Yi of Hedong became Prince of He as Qi.

sentences.zh: 十七男絢封衡王，十九男纁封會王，二十男綰封福王，二十一紘男封撫王，二十三男緄封岳王，二十四男紳封袁王，二十五男綸封桂王，二十七男繟封翼王，彌臣國嗣王道勿禮封彌臣國王。

translations.literal: The seventeenth son Xuan was enfeoffed Prince of Heng; the nineteenth son Xun Prince of Hui; the twentieth Guan Prince of Fu; the twenty-first Hong Prince of Fu; the twenty-third Lun Prince of Yue; the twenty-fourth Shen Prince of Yuan; the twenty-fifth Lun Prince of Gui; the twenty-seventh Chan Prince of Yi; the heir of Michin, Dao Wul-li, was enfeoffed King of Michin.
translations.idiomatic: A batch of younger princes and a Michin heir received titles.

sentences.zh: 西平郡王晟男左羽林大將軍願襲封岐公，食邑三千戶。

translations.literal: The son of Prince of Xiping Sheng, Left General of the Left Forest Guard Yuan, inherited enfeoffment as Duke of Qi with a fief of three thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng's son Yuan inherited the Qi dukedom with three thousand households.

sentences.zh: 戊申，詔以冊太子禮畢，赦京城系囚，大辟降從流，流以下減一等。

translations.literal: On wushen an edict, because the heir's investiture rites were complete, pardoned capital prisoners in the capital — great execution reduced to exile, exile and below reduced one grade.
translations.idiomatic: Capital prisoners were partially pardoned after the heir's enthronement rites on wushen.

sentences.zh: 以給事中陸質、中書舍人崔樞並為太子侍讀。

translations.literal: Supervisor of Attendants Lu Zhi and Secretariat Drafter Cui Shu were both made lecturers to the heir.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi and Cui Shu became tutors to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，封太子男甯、寬、宥、察、寰、寮等六人為郡王，並食邑三千戶。

translations.literal: On gengxu the heir's sons Ning, Kuan, You, Cha, Huan, and Liao were enfeoffed princes of commanderies, each with a fief of three thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Six of the heir's sons became commandery princes on gengxu.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，贈吐蕃使、工部侍郎、兼御史大夫張薦禮部尚書。

translations.literal: On guichou Zhang Jian, late envoy to Tibet, Vice Minister of Works and concurrent Censor-in-Chief, was posthumously made Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jian was posthumously honored on guichou.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，罷萬安監牧。

translations.literal: On bingyin the Wan'an supervisory pasture was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The Wan'an imperial pasture was shut on bingyin.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，以杭州刺史韓皋為尚書右丞。

translations.literal: On wuchen Han Gao, prefect of Hangzhou, was made Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Han Gao entered the central administration on wuchen.

sentences.zh: 五月己巳，以右金吾衛大將軍范希朝為右神策統軍，充左右神策、京西諸城鎮行營兵馬節度使。

translations.literal: Fifth month, jisi — Right General of the Right Golden Guard Fan Xichao was made commanding general of the Right Divine Strategy Army and commissioner of the Left and Right Divine Strategy and western capital garrison campaign forces.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Xichao took command of the Shence armies in the fifth month.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，以邕管經略使韋丹為河南少尹，以萬年縣令房啟為容管經略招討使。

translations.literal: On dingchou Wei Dan, Yong circuit commissioner, was made Vice Governor of Henan; Fang Qi, magistrate of Wannian, was made Rongguan pacification and campaign commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Dan and Fang Qi received southern posts on dingchou.

sentences.zh: 癸未，以郴州司馬鄭余慶為尚書左丞。

translations.literal: On guiwei Zheng Yuqing, staff officer of Chenzhou, was made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yuqing became left vice director on guiwei.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，以檢校司空、忽汗州都督、渤海國王大嵩璘檢校司徒。

translations.literal: On jiachen King Daesung of Parhae, acting Master of Works and governor of Hohon, was made acting Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: The Parhae king was promoted on jiachen.

sentences.zh: 承徽王氏、趙氏可昭儀，崔氏、楊氏可充儀，王氏可昭媛，王氏可昭容，牛氏可修儀，張氏可美人。

translations.literal: Lady Wang and Lady Zhao of Chenghui could be Brilliant Companion; Ladies Cui and Yang could be Filling Companion; Lady Wang could be Brilliant Beauty; another Lady Wang could be Brilliant Countenance; Lady Niu could be Cultivated Beauty; Lady Zhang could be Beauty.
translations.idiomatic: Several palace ladies received new rank titles.

sentences.zh: 以右丞韓皋為鄂嶽沔蘄都團練觀察使。

translations.literal: Right Vice Director Han Gao was made regimental and observation commissioner of E, Yue, Mian, and Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Han Gao left the capital for the E-Yue command.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，升襄州為大都督府。

translations.literal: On dinghai Xiangzhou was elevated to a great metropolitan prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangyang became a great metropolitan prefecture on dinghai.

sentences.zh: 臨漢縣仍徙于鄧城。

translations.literal: Linhan county was again moved to Dengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Linhan county seat was relocated to Dengcheng.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，以鹽鐵轉運使副王叔文為戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: On xinmao Wang Shuwen, vice commissioner of salt and iron transport, was made Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shuwen became vice minister of revenue on xinmao.

sentences.zh: 六月丙申，詔二十一年十月已前百姓所欠諸色課利、租賦、錢帛，共五十二萬六千八百四十一貫、石、匹、束，並宜除免。

translations.literal: Sixth month, bingshen — an edict: all levies, rents, and cash and silk owed by the people before the tenth month of year 21, totaling 526,841 strings, piculs, bolts, and bundles, were all to be remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Over half a million units of back taxes were forgiven on bingshen.

sentences.zh: 七月戊辰朔，吐蕃使論悉諾來朝貢。

translations.literal: Seventh month, wuchen new moon — the Tibetan envoy Lun Senor came to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: A Tibetan envoy presented tribute at the seventh-month audience.

sentences.zh: 丙子，鄆州李師古加檢校侍中。

translations.literal: On bingzi Li Shigu of Yanzhou was made acting Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shigu received an honorary palace title on bingzi.

sentences.zh: 贈故忠州別駕陸贄兵部尚書，諡曰宣；

translations.literal: The late Vice Prefect of Zhongzhou Lu Zhi was posthumously made Vice Minister of War, posthumous name Xuan;
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi was posthumously honored as Vice Minister of War with the posthumous name Xuan;

sentences.zh: 贈故道州刺史陽城為左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: the late Prefect of Daozhou Yang Cheng was posthumously made Left Regular Cavalry Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Cheng was posthumously made Left Regular Cavalry Attendant.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，以戶部侍郎潘孟陽為度支鹽鐵轉運使副。

translations.literal: On wuyin Pan Mengyang, Vice Minister of Revenue, was made vice commissioner of revenue, salt, iron, and transport.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Mengyang joined the fiscal commission on wuyin.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，關東蝗食田稼。

translations.literal: On bingxu locusts in the east ate the fields.
translations.idiomatic: Locusts ravaged eastern crops on bingxu.

sentences.zh: 癸已，橫海軍節度伎、滄州刺史程懷信卒，以其子副使執恭起復滄州刺史、橫海軍節度使。

translations.literal: On guisi Cheng Huaixin, military commissioner of the Transocean Army and prefect of Cang, died; his son Vice Commissioner Zhigong was recalled from mourning to succeed as prefect of Cang and military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Huaixin died; his son Zhigong inherited the Transocean command on guisi.

sentences.zh: 甲午，度支使杜祐奏：「太倉見米八十萬石，貯來十五年，東渭橋米四十五萬石，支諸軍皆不悅。

translations.literal: On jiawu Revenue Commissioner Du You memorialized: "In the Grand Granary there are presently 800,000 piculs, stored fifteen years; at Dongwei Bridge 450,000 piculs — paying out to the armies, none are pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Du You reported huge old grain stores that troops refused to eat on jiawu.

sentences.zh: 今歲豐阜，請權停北河轉運，於濱河州府和糴二十萬石，以救農傷之弊。

translations.literal: This year is abundant; I ask to suspend temporarily north-river transport and purchase in harmony 200,000 piculs in riverine prefectures and circuits, to relieve the harm to agriculture."
translations.idiomatic: He proposed halting northern transport and local purchase to ease rural distress.

sentences.zh: 」乃下百僚議，議者同異，不決而止。

translations.literal: The matter was sent down for the hundred officials to debate; debaters differed, and it stopped undecided.
translations.idiomatic: Officials split on the plan and it died in debate.

sentences.zh: 乙未，詔：「朕承九聖之烈，荷萬邦之重。

translations.literal: On yiwei an edict: "I inherit the glory of the nine sages and bear the weight of ten thousand states.
translations.idiomatic: An edict on yiwei opened with the emperor's sense of unworthy burden:

sentences.zh: 顧以寡德，涉道未明，虔恭寅畏，懼不克荷。

translations.literal: Looking on my slight virtue, my path in the Way is not yet clear; reverent and cautious, I fear I cannot bear it.
translations.idiomatic: he confessed weak virtue and fear of failing the throne.

sentences.zh: 恐上墜祖宗之訓，下貽卿士之憂，夙夜祗勤，如臨淵穀。

translations.literal: I fear above I will drop the ancestors' instruction and below leave worry to the ministers; morning and night reverent diligence, as if facing an abyss or ravine.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke of dreading to disappoint ancestors and ministers alike.

sentences.zh: 而積疾未復，至於經時，怡神保和，常所不暇。

translations.literal: Yet accumulated illness is not recovered, reaching across seasons; nurturing spirit and preserving harmony is often what I have no leisure for.
translations.idiomatic: Chronic illness, he said, left no strength for rule.

sentences.zh: 永惟四方之大，萬務之殷，不躬不親，慮有曠廢。

translations.literal: Ever considering the vastness of the four quarters and the multitude of affairs — if I do not personally attend, I fear there will be neglect.
translations.idiomatic: He feared the realm's business could not wait on his recovery.

sentences.zh: 加以山陵有日，霖潦逾旬，是用儆於朕心，以答天戒。

translations.literal: Moreover the mountain tomb has its day; heavy rains exceed ten days — therefore I am warned in heart to answer Heaven's admonition.
translations.idiomatic: Impending burial and floods moved him to heed Heaven's warning.

sentences.zh: 其軍國政事，宜令皇太子勾當。

translations.literal: Military and civil affairs should be ordered handled by the crown prince."
translations.idiomatic: He entrusted all state affairs to the crown prince. Thus ended the edict.

sentences.zh: 」時上久疾，不復延納宰臣共論大政。

translations.literal: At the time the Emperor had long been ill and no longer received and admitted councillors to discuss great affairs together.
translations.idiomatic: The sick emperor had ceased to meet his chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 事無巨細皆決于李忠言、王伾、王叔文。

translations.literal: Nothing great or small was all decided by Li Zhongyan, Wang Pi, and Wang Shuwen.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhongyan, Wang Pi, and Wang Shuwen decided everything.

sentences.zh: 物論喧雜，以為不可。

translations.literal: Public opinion was noisy and confused; it was held impossible.
translations.idiomatic: Court opinion condemned the arrangement as unworkable.

sentences.zh: 籓鎮屢上箋于皇太子，指三豎之撓政，故有是詔。

translations.literal: The frontier commands repeatedly sent memorials to the crown prince, pointing to the three eunuchs' interference in government — hence this edict.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial armies blamed eunuch meddling and forced the transfer edict.

sentences.zh: 乙太常卿杜黃裳為門下侍郎，左金吾衛大軍袁滋為中書侍郎，並同中書門下平章事；

translations.literal: On yisi, Minister of Rites Du Huangchang was made Vice Director of the Chancellery; Left Golden Guard Grand General Yuan Zi was made Vice Director of the Secretariat; both were Grand Councillors;
translations.idiomatic: Du Huangchang and Yuan Zi entered the council on yisi;

sentences.zh: 鄭珣瑜為吏部尚書，高郢刑部尚書，並罷知政事。

translations.literal: Zheng Qionyu was made Minister of Personnel, Gao Ying Minister of Justice; both ceased handling administration.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Qionyu and Gao Ying left the council.

sentences.zh: 皇太子見百僚於朝堂。

translations.literal: The crown prince received the hundred officials in the court hall.
translations.idiomatic: The heir held court for the bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 丙申，皇太子于麟德殿西亭見奏事官。

translations.literal: On bingshen the crown prince at the west pavilion of Linde Hall received officials who presented business.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen he heard petitions at Linde's west pavilion.

sentences.zh: 八月丁酉朔。

translations.literal: Eighth month, dingyou new moon.
translations.idiomatic: The eighth month opened on dingyou.

sentences.zh: 庚子，詔：「惟皇天佑命烈祖，誕受方國，九聖儲祉，萬邦咸休。

translations.literal: On gengzi an edict: "Only the August Heaven blesses and orders the glorious ancestor, who received the regions and states; the nine sages stored blessing; ten thousand states all rest.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi an abdication edict invoked Heaven's mandate on the Tang line:

sentences.zh: 肆予一人，獲績丕業，嚴恭守位，不遑暇逸。

translations.literal: I alone have obtained and continued the great enterprise, stern and reverent in keeping the throne, with no leisure to rest.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor confessed illness and inability to sustain rule alone.

sentences.zh: 而天佑不降，疾恙無瘳，將何以奉宗廟之靈，展郊、禋之禮！

translations.literal: Yet Heaven's blessing does not descend; illness is not cured — how shall I serve the ancestral temple's spirits, or perform suburban and border sacrifices!
translations.idiomatic: He asked how he could sacrifice while still gravely ill.

sentences.zh: 疇咨庶尹，對越上玄，內愧於朕心，上畏於天命。

translations.literal: I consult the many directors and face the Supreme Heaven; inwardly I am ashamed in heart, upward I fear Heaven's mandate.
translations.idiomatic: He professed shame before Heaven and the ministers.

sentences.zh: 夙夜祗慄，深惟永圖。

translations.literal: Morning and night reverent fear, deeply pondering the long plan.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke of sleepless dread for the realm's future.

sentences.zh: 一日萬機，不可以久曠；

translations.literal: Ten thousand affairs in a day cannot long be vacant;
translations.idiomatic: The throne could not stay empty, he said;

sentences.zh: 天工人代，不可以久違。

translations.literal: Heaven's work and man's replacement cannot long be violated.
translations.idiomatic: nor could the mandate wait on his recovery.

sentences.zh: 皇太子純睿哲溫文，寬和仁惠，孝友之德，愛敬之誠，通乎神明，格於上下。

translations.literal: The crown prince Chun is wise and perspicacious, warm in culture, broad and harmonious, benevolent and kind; filial and brotherly virtue, loving and reverent sincerity, penetrate the spirits and reach above and below.
translations.idiomatic: He praised Prince Chun's virtue as fit for rule.

sentences.zh: 是用法皇王至公之道，遵父子傳歸之制，付之重器，以撫兆人。

translations.literal: Therefore I use the imperial king's utmost public Way, follow father-and-son transmission's system, entrust the great vessel, to comfort the trillion people.
translations.idiomatic: He would abdicate by the ancient public transfer of the vessel.

sentences.zh: 必能宣祖宗之重光，荷天地之休命，奉若成憲，永綏四方。

translations.literal: He will surely be able to proclaim the ancestors' heavy radiance, bear Heaven-and-earth's fine mandate, follow and accord with the completed statutes, and forever pacify the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Chun, he vowed, would restore Tang glory and pacify the realm.

sentences.zh: 宜令皇太子即皇帝位，朕稱太上皇，居興慶宮，制稱誥。

translations.literal: It is fitting to order the crown prince immediately to take the imperial throne; I shall be called Retired Emperor, dwelling in Xingqing Palace; my documents shall be called Proclamations."
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Chun enthroned and himself retired to Xingqing as Taishang Huang. Thus ended the edict.

sentences.zh: 」辛丑，誥：「有天下傳歸於子，前王之制也。

translations.literal: On xinchou a proclamation: "Having the realm and transmitting it to one's son is the former kings' system.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou a proclamation framed abdication as ancient custom:

sentences.zh: 欽若大典，斯為至公，式揚耿光，用體文德。

translations.literal: Reverently according with the great canon, this is utmost publicness; thereby to raise bright glory and embody civil virtue.
translations.idiomatic: it cast the transfer as supreme public duty.

sentences.zh: 朕獲奉宗廟，臨禦萬方，降疾不瘳，庶政多闕。

translations.literal: I have obtained service to the ancestral temple and face and rule ten thousand regions; descending illness is not cured; many ordinary affairs are lacking.
translations.idiomatic: Illness, he said, had left government in disarray.

sentences.zh: 乃命元子，代予守邦，爰以令辰，光膺冊禮，宜以今月九日冊皇帝于宣政殿。

translations.literal: Therefore I order the eldest son to guard the state in my stead; on this honored day he brightly receives the investiture rites — on the ninth of this month the Emperor is to be enfeoffed at Xuanzheng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Chun's enthronement was set for the ninth at Xuanzheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 國有大命，恩俾惟新，宜因紀元之慶，用覃在宥之澤。

translations.literal: The state has a great mandate; grace should renew all — it is fitting, because of the rejoicing in changing the era, to extend the mercy of release within the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: A new reign would bring a general pardon.

sentences.zh: 宜改貞元二十一年為永貞元年。

translations.literal: Zhenyuan 21 should be changed to Yongzhen 1.
translations.idiomatic: The era name became Yongzhen.

sentences.zh: 自貞元二十一年八月五日已前，天下死罪降從流，流以下遞減一等。

translations.literal: From before the fifth day of the eighth month of Zhenyuan 21, empire-wide death sentences were reduced to exile; exile and below were reduced one grade in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Capital crimes were commuted in the abdication amnesty. Thus ended the proclamation.

sentences.zh: 」誥立良娣王氏為太上皇后，良媛董氏為太上皇德妃。

translations.literal: A proclamation installed Lady Wang, Senior Consort, as Retired Empress, and Lady Dong, Junior Consort, as Retired Emperor's Virtuous Consort.
translations.idiomatic: Wang and Dong received retired-harem ranks.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，貶右散騎常侍王伾為開州司馬，前戶部侍郎、度支鹽鐵轉運使王叔文為渝州司戶。

translations.literal: On renyin Right Regular Cavalry Attendant Wang Pi was demoted to staff officer of Kaizhou; former Vice Minister of Revenue and revenue, salt, iron, and transport commissioner Wang Shuwen was demoted to census officer of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pi and Wang Shuwen were exiled on renyin.

sentences.zh: 正月丙寅朔，皇帝率百僚上太上皇尊號曰應乾聖壽。

translations.literal: First month, bingyin new moon — the Emperor led the hundred officials to present to the Retired Emperor the honorific title Responding to Heaven, Sagely Longevity.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong offered his father the honorific Responding to Heaven, Sagely Longevity.

sentences.zh: 甲申，太上皇崩于興慶宮之咸寧殿，享年四十六歲。

translations.literal: On jiashen the Retired Emperor died in Xianning Hall of Xingqing Palace, aged forty-six.
translations.idiomatic: Shunzong died at forty-six in Xingqing Palace on jiashen.

sentences.zh: 六月乙卯，皇帝率群臣上大行太上皇諡曰至德大聖大安孝皇帝，廟號順宗。

translations.literal: Sixth month, yimao — the Emperor led the ministers to present on the late Retired Emperor the posthumous title To the Utmost Virtue Great Sage Great Peace Filial; temple name Shunzong.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the court fixed Shunzong's posthumous name and temple title.

sentences.zh: 秋七月壬申，葬于豐陵。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, renshen — buried at Feng Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: He was buried at Fengling in the seventh month.

sentences.zh: 史臣韓愈曰：順宗之為太子也，留心藝術，善隸書。

translations.literal: Historian Han Yu said: In Shunzong's time as heir he devoted his heart to the arts and was skilled at clerical script.
translations.idiomatic: 【Historian's appraisal】 Han Yu wrote that as heir Shunzong cultivated the arts and excelled at clerical script.

sentences.zh: 德宗工為詩，每賜大臣方鎮詩制，必命書之。

translations.literal: Dezong was skilled at composing poetry; whenever he bestowed poems and orders on great ministers and frontier commissioners, he always ordered the heir to write them out.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong had him copy every poem sent to ministers and generals.

sentences.zh: 性寬仁有斷，禮重師傅，必先致拜。

translations.literal: His nature was broad and benevolent yet decisive; he honored teachers with ritual and always bowed first.
translations.idiomatic: He was gentle but firm and ceremoniously honored his tutors.

sentences.zh: 從幸奉天，賊泚逼迫，常身先禁旅，乘城拒戰，督勵將士，無不奮激。

translations.literal: Following the fortune to Fengtian, when rebel Zhu pressed close, he often personally led the palace guard, mounted the wall to repel battle, and urged the officers and soldiers — none did not strive fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: At Fengtian he fought on the walls and roused the guards against Zhu Ci.

sentences.zh: 德宗在位歲久，稍不假權宰相。

translations.literal: Dezong's years on the throne were long; gradually he did not lend authority to chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Dezong's reign chancellors held little real power.

sentences.zh: 左右幸臣如裴延齡、李齊運、韋渠牟等，因間用事，刻下取功，而排陷陸贄、張滂輩，人不敢言，太子從容論爭，故卒不任延齡、渠牟為相。

translations.literal: Favored attendants at his side such as Pei Yanling, Li Qiyun, and Wei Qumou, exploiting intervals, wielded affairs, carved the lower to win merit, and drove out Lu Zhi, Zhang Pang, and their kind — men did not dare speak; the heir calmly argued and debated — therefore in the end Yanling and Qumou were not made chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: He alone spoke against favorites who ruined Lu Zhi and blocked their rise to the council.

sentences.zh: 嘗侍宴魚藻宮。

translations.literal: He once attended a banquet at Fish-Algae Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Once at Fish-Algae Palace he attended a banquet.

sentences.zh: 張水嬉，綵艦雕靡，宮人引舟為棹歌，絲竹間發，德宗歡甚，太子引詩人「好樂無荒」為對。

translations.literal: They spread water games; colored ships carved and lavish; palace women drew boats and made oar-songs; silk and bamboo sounded between — Dezong was very pleased; the heir cited the poet's "love pleasure but do not waste" in reply.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong reveled at water games, the heir quoted the Odes on restraint.

sentences.zh: 每於敷奏，未嘗以顏色假借宦官。

translations.literal: Whenever in memorials to the throne, he never lent his countenance to eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: In audience he never showed eunuchs a compliant face.

sentences.zh: 居儲位二十年，天下陰受其賜。

translations.literal: Dwelling in the stored position twenty years, the realm in secret received his bounty.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty years as heir, the empire quietly benefited from him.

sentences.zh: 惜乎寢疾踐祚，近習弄權；

translations.literal: Alas — he fell ill upon taking the throne; close attendants played with power;
translations.idiomatic: Alas, sickness at accession let intimates seize power;

sentences.zh: 而能傳政元良，克昌運祚，賢哉！

translations.literal: yet he could transmit rule to the primary heir and splendidly continue the mandate — how worthy!
translations.idiomatic: yet he passed the throne to a worthy son and saved the dynasty — how worthy a ruler!

sentences.zh: 憲宗憲宗聖神章武孝皇帝諱純，順宗長子也，母曰莊憲王太后。

translations.literal: Xianzong — Emperor Xianzong, Sagely Spirit Manifest Martial Filial, taboo name Chun, eldest son of Shunzong; mother the Honored Empress Zhuangxian Wang.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong, the Filial Emperor Chun, was Shunzong's eldest son; his mother was Empress Zhuangxian.

sentences.zh: 大曆十三年二月生於長安之東內。

translations.literal: Second month, Dali 13, born in the Eastern Inner Palace at Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was born in Chang'an's eastern palace in Dali 13.

sentences.zh: 六七歲時，德宗抱置膝上，問曰：「汝誰子，在吾懷？

translations.literal: When six or seven years old, Dezong held him on his knee and asked: "Whose child are you, in my embrace?
translations.idiomatic: At six or seven Dezong set him on his knee and asked whose child he was.

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「是第三天子。

translations.literal: "He replied: "I am the third Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "The third Son of Heaven."

sentences.zh: 」德宗異而憐之。

translations.literal: Dezong marveled and pitied him.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong was struck and fond of the boy.

sentences.zh: 貞元四年六月，封廣陵王。

translations.literal: Sixth month, Zhenyuan 4 — enfeoffed Prince of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: He became Prince of Guangling in Zhenyuan 4.

sentences.zh: 順宗即位之年四月，冊為皇太子。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the year Shunzong took the throne, he was enfeoffed crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: He was made crown prince in Shunzong's fourth month.

sentences.zh: 七月乙未，權勾當軍國政事。

translations.literal: Seventh month, yiwei — provisionally handled military and civil affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he was regent for state affairs.

sentences.zh: 八月丁酉朔，受內禪。

translations.literal: Eighth month, dingyou new moon — received the inner abdication.
translations.idiomatic: He received the inner abdication at the eighth-month new moon.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，即皇帝位於宣政殿。

translations.literal: On yisi he took the imperial throne at Xuanzheng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He ascended at Xuanzheng Hall on yisi.

sentences.zh: 先是，連月霖雨，上即位之日晴霽，人情欣悅。

translations.literal: Earlier, for months it had rained; on the day the Emperor took the throne the sky cleared — people's hearts were glad.
translations.idiomatic: Rain had drenched the capital for months; his accession day dawned clear, to popular joy.

sentences.zh: 丙午，升平公主進女口十五人，上曰：「太上皇不受獻，朕何敢違！

translations.literal: On bingwu Princess Shengping presented fifteen female attendants; the Emperor said: "The Retired Emperor did not accept presentations — how dare I disobey!
translations.idiomatic: He refused fifteen women from Princess Shengping, citing his father's example:

sentences.zh: 其還郭氏。

translations.literal: Return them to the Guo clan."
translations.idiomatic: Send them back to the Guo family. Thus ended the edict.

sentences.zh: 」丁未，始禦紫宸對百僚。

translations.literal: On dingwei he first took Zichen and faced the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei he held his first audience at Zichen Hall.

sentences.zh: 己酉，以道州刺史路怒為邕管經略使。

translations.literal: On jiyou Lu Nu, prefect of Daozhou, was made Yongguan pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Nu became Yongguan commissioner on jiyou.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，荊南獻龜二，詔曰：「朕以寡昧，纂承丕業，永思理本，所寶惟賢。

translations.literal: On gengxu Jingnan presented two tortoises; an edict said: "I with slight understanding inherit the great enterprise; forever thinking of governance's root, what I treasure is only the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu he rejected tortoise omens, declaring he valued men over prodigies:

sentences.zh: 至如嘉禾神芝，奇禽異獸，蓋王化之虛美也。

translations.literal: As for fine grain and divine fungus, strange birds and exotic beasts — these are empty adornments of kingly transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Auspicious grain and beasts were empty pageantry, he said.

sentences.zh: 所以光武形於詔令，《春秋》不書祥瑞，朕誠薄德，思及前人。

translations.literal: Therefore Guangwu set it forth in edicts; the Spring and Autumn Annals do not record auspicious omens — I truly have thin virtue and think of former men.
translations.idiomatic: He cited Guangwu and the Spring and Autumn to shun flattery by omens.

sentences.zh: 自今已後，所有祥瑞，但令准式申報有司，不得上聞；

translations.literal: From now onward, all auspicious omens are only to be reported by standard form to the relevant offices; they must not be reported upward;
translations.idiomatic: Hereafter omens were to be filed with local offices only, not announced to the throne;

sentences.zh: 其奇禽異獸，亦宜停進。

translations.literal: strange birds and exotic beasts should also cease being presented.
translations.idiomatic: and exotic animals were barred from court. Thus ended the edict.

sentences.zh: 」癸丑，劍南西川節度使、檢校太尉、中書令、南康郡王韋皋薨。

translations.literal: On guichou Wei Gao, military commissioner of southwestern Sichuan, acting Grand General, Grand Preceptor, and Prince of Nankang, died.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Gao, the great western commander, died on guichou.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，以常州刺史穆贊為宣歙池觀察使，以前宣歙觀察使崔衍為工部尚書。

translations.literal: On jiayin Mu Zan, prefect of Changzhou, was made Xuanchi-Chi observer; former Xuanchi-Chi observer Cui Yan was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Mu Zan and Cui Yan changed Huai-nan posts on jiayin.

sentences.zh: 己未，以中書侍郎、平章事袁滋為劍南東西兩川、山南西道安撫大使，時昌韋皋卒，劉辟據蜀邀節鉞故也。

translations.literal: On jiwei Yuan Zi, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councillor, was made pacification grand commissioner of eastern and western Sichuan and southwestern Shannan — at the time because Wei Gao had died and Liu Pi held Shu and sought the commander's seal.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zi was sent west because Liu Pi seized Sichuan after Wei Gao's death.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，太上皇誥冊良娣王氏為太上皇后。

translations.literal: On xinyou the Retired Emperor's proclamation enfeoffed Senior Consort Lady Wang as Retired Empress.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wang was made retired empress by proclamation on xinyou.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，以朝請大夫、守尚書左丞、輕車都尉、賜紫金魚袋鄭余慶同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: On guihai Zheng Yuqing, Grand Master for Court Audience, acting Left Vice Director, Light-Carriage Commandant, and bearer of the purple-gold fish bag, was made Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yuqing entered the council on guihai.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，以饒州刺史李吉甫為考功郎中，夔州刺史唐次為吏部郎中。

translations.literal: On bingyin Li Jifu, prefect of Raozhou, was made bureau director in the Ministry of Personnel; Tang Ci, prefect of Kuizhou, was made bureau director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jifu and Tang Ci became personnel directors on bingyin.

sentences.zh: 並知制誥。

translations.literal: Both were also drafters of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Both also drafted imperial prose.

sentences.zh: 九月丁卯朔。

translations.literal: Ninth month, dingmao new moon.
translations.idiomatic: The ninth month opened on dingmao.

sentences.zh: 己巳，罷教坊樂人授正員官之制。

translations.literal: On jisi the practice of granting regular-rank offices to music girls of the teaching workshops was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Court musicians lost the right to regular civil rank on jisi.

sentences.zh: 辛未，河陽三城節度使元韶卒。

translations.literal: On xinwei Yuan Shao, military commissioner of the Three Cities of Heyang, died.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao of Heyang died on xinwei.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，以陳州刺史孟元陽為懷州刺史、河陽三城孟懷節度使。

translations.literal: On guiyou Meng Yuanyang, prefect of Chen, was made prefect of Huai and military commissioner of the Three Cities of Meng-Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Yuanyang succeeded the Heyang command on guiyou.

sentences.zh: 丙子，敕申光蔡、陳許兩道比遭亢旱，宜加賑恤，申、光、蔡賑米十萬石，陳、許五萬石。

translations.literal: On bingzi an order: Shen-Guang-Cai and Chen-Xu circuits had lately suffered severe drought — relief should be increased; Shen, Guang, and Cai were given 100,000 piculs of relief grain; Chen and Xu 50,000.
translations.idiomatic: Drought relief grain was allotted to central circuits on bingzi.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，前戶部侍郎蔡弁卒。

translations.literal: On dingchou former Vice Minister of Revenue Cai Bian died.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Bian died on dingchou.

sentences.zh: 襄州于頔進鷹，詔還之。

translations.literal: Yu Di of Xiangzhou presented hawks; an edict returned them.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Di's hawk tribute was sent back.

sentences.zh: 己卯，京西神策行營節度行軍司馬韓泰貶撫州刺史，司封郎中韓曄貶池州刺史，禮部員外郎柳宗元貶邵州刺史，屯田員外郎劉禹錫貶連州刺史，坐交王叔文也。

translations.literal: On jimao Han Tai, staff officer of the Jingxi Shence campaign command, was demoted to prefect of Fu; Han Ye, bureau director in the Ministry of Rites, to Chi; Liu Zongyuan, outer bureau director in the Ministry of Rites, to Shao; Liu Yuxi, outer bureau director in the Ministry of Revenue, to Lian — all for associating with Wang Shuwen.
translations.idiomatic: Four Wang Shuwen allies were exiled to prefectures on jimao.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，給事中陸質卒。

translations.literal: On xinsi Supervisor of Attendants Lu Zhi died.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi died on xinsi.

sentences.zh: 冬十月丙申朔。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, bingshen new moon.
translations.idiomatic: The tenth month opened on bingshen.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，集百僚發曾太皇太后沈氏哀于肅章門外。

translations.literal: On dingyou the hundred officials were assembled to begin mourning for the late Grand Empress Dowager Shen outside Suzhang Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Court mourning for Empress Shen began outside Suzhang Gate on dingyou.

sentences.zh: 檢校司空兼右僕射、同中書門下平章事、魏國公賈耽卒。

translations.literal: Acting Master of Works and concurrent Right Vice Director, Grand Councillor, Duke of Wei Jia Dan died.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Councillor Jia Dan died.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，以宰臣劍南安撫使袁滋檢校吏部尚書、同中書門下平章事、成都尹、劍南西川節度觀察等使，以西川行軍司馬齊辟為給事中。

translations.literal: On wuxu Councillor and Sichuan pacification commissioner Yuan Zi was made acting Minister of Personnel, Grand Councillor, Governor of Chengdu, and Sichuan observation commissioner; Sichuan campaign staff officer Liu Pi was made Supervisor of Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zi took Sichuan; Liu Pi was promoted on wuxu.

sentences.zh: 舒王誼薨。

translations.literal: Prince of Shu Yi died.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yi of Shu died.

sentences.zh: 庚子，南詔使趙迦寬來赴山陵。

translations.literal: On gengzi the Nanzhao envoy Zhao Jiakuan came to attend the mountain tomb.
translations.idiomatic: A Nanzhao envoy came for the imperial funeral on gengzi.

sentences.zh: 浙東觀察使賈全卒。

translations.literal: Zhedong observer Jia Quan died.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Quan, Zhedong observer, died.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，吐蕃使論乞縷貢助山陵金銀衣服。

translations.literal: On xinchou the Tibetan envoy Lun Qilü presented gold, silver, and clothing to assist the mountain tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet sent funeral gifts on xinchou.

sentences.zh: 太常上大行曾太皇太后沈氏諡曰睿真皇后。

translations.literal: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices presented on the late Grand Empress Dowager Shen the posthumous title Empress Ruizhen.
translations.idiomatic: Shen received the posthumous title Empress Ruizhen.

sentences.zh: 丙午，以華州刺史楊于陵為越州刺史、浙東觀察使。

translations.literal: On bingwu Yang Yuling, prefect of Hua, was made prefect of Yue and Zhedong observer.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yuling went to Zhedong on bingwu.

sentences.zh: 丁未，改桂州純化縣為慕化縣，蒙州純義縣為正義縣。

translations.literal: On dingwei Chunhua county of Guizhou was renamed Muhua county; Chunyi county of Mengzhou was renamed Zhengyi county.
translations.idiomatic: Two counties were renamed on dingwei.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，葬德宗皇帝于崇陵。

translations.literal: On yiyou Emperor Dezong was buried at Chong Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong was buried at Chongling on yiyou.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，以刑部尚書高郢為華州刺史、潼關防禦、鎮國軍使，御史中丞李鄘為京兆尹。

translations.literal: On jiayin Gao Ying, Minister of Justice, was made prefect of Hua, Tongguan defender, and Zhenguo army commissioner; Vice Censor-in-Chief Li Yong was made Metropolitan Governor.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Ying and Li Yong took western posts on jiayin.

sentences.zh: 貶京兆尹王權為雅王傅。

translations.literal: Metropolitan Governor Wang Quan was demoted to tutor of the Prince of Ya.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Quan was demoted from the capital magistracy.

sentences.zh: 久雨，京師鹽貴，出庫鹽二萬石，糶以惠民。

translations.literal: Long rain — salt in the capital was dear; 20,000 piculs were taken from the storehouses and sold cheap to benefit the people.
translations.idiomatic: The court sold reserve salt cheaply after prolonged rain inflated prices.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，祔睿真皇后神主、德宗皇帝神主于太廟。

translations.literal: On yisi the spirit tablets of Empress Ruizhen and Emperor Dezong were enshrined in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Ruizhen and Dezong entered the ancestral temple on yisi.

sentences.zh: 壬申，貶正議大夫、中書侍郎、平章事韋執誼為崖州司馬，以交王叔文也。

translations.literal: On renshen Wei Zhiyi, Grand Master of Correct Counsel, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councillor, was demoted to staff officer of Yazhou — for associating with Wang Shuwen.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhiyi was exiled to Yazhou on renshen for the Shuwen faction.

sentences.zh: 潤、池、揚、楚、湖、杭、睦、江等州旱。

translations.literal: Run, Chi, Yang, Chu, Hu, Hang, Mu, Jiang, and other prefectures suffered drought.
translations.idiomatic: Drought struck the lower Yangzi region.

sentences.zh: 貶劍南西川節度使袁滋為吉州刺史，以其慰撫三川逗留不進故也。

translations.literal: Sichuan military commissioner Yuan Zi was demoted to prefect of Ji — because in comforting the Three Gorges he lingered and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zi was punished for stalling against Liu Pi.

sentences.zh: 以左驍衛將軍李演為夏州刺史、夏綏銀等州節度使，以右庶子武元衡為御史中丞。

translations.literal: Left General of the Left Valiant Guard Li Yan was made prefect of Xia and commissioner of Xia, Sui, and Yin; Right Subordinate Heir-Apparent Wu Yuanheng was made Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yan and Wu Yuanheng received frontier and censor posts.

sentences.zh: 己卯，再貶撫州刺史韓泰為虔州司馬，河中少尹陳諫台州司馬，邵州刺史柳宗元為永州司馬，連州刺史劉禹錫朗州司馬，池州刺史韓曄饒州司馬，和州刺史淩准連州司馬，岳州刺史程異郴州司馬，皆坐交王叔文。

translations.literal: On jimao Han Tai, demoted from prefect of Fu, was again demoted to staff officer of Qian; Chen Jian, Vice Governor of Hezhong, to Taizhou; Liu Zongyuan, prefect of Shao, to Yongzhou; Liu Yuxi, prefect of Lian, to Langzhou; Han Ye, prefect of Chi, to Raozhou; Ling Zhun, prefect of He, to Lianzhou; Cheng Yi, prefect of Yue, to Chenzhou — all for associating with Wang Shuwen.
translations.idiomatic: Eight Shuwen allies were demoted again from prefect to staff officer on jimao.

sentences.zh: 初貶刺史，物議罪之，故再加貶竄。

translations.literal: At first they were demoted to prefects; public opinion blamed this — therefore they were again demoted and cast out.
translations.idiomatic: Public outcry forced a harsher second exile.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，宣、撫、和、郴、郢、袁、衢七州旱。

translations.literal: On xinsi Xuan, Fu, He, Chen, E, Yuan, and Qu seven prefectures suffered drought.
translations.idiomatic: Seven more circuits reported drought on xinsi.

sentences.zh: 壬午，吏部尚書鄭珣瑜卒。

translations.literal: On renwu Minister of Personnel Zheng Qionyu died.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Qionyu died on renwu.

sentences.zh: 甲申，以湖南觀察使楊憑為洪州刺史、江西觀察使，以虢州刺史薛蘋為潭州刺史、湖南觀察使。

translations.literal: On jiashen Yang Ping, Hunan observer, was made prefect of Hong and Jiangxi observer; Xue Pin, prefect of Guo, was made prefect of Tan and Hunan observer.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ping and Xue Pin changed southern commands on jiashen.

sentences.zh: 鄂、嶽、婺、衡等州旱。

translations.literal: E, Yue, Wu, and Heng prefectures suffered drought.
translations.idiomatic: More drought in the middle Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，宣歙觀察使穆贊卒。

translations.literal: On guisi Xuanchi observer Mu Zan died.
translations.idiomatic: Mu Zan died on guisi.

sentences.zh: 十二月丙申朔。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, bingshen new moon.
translations.idiomatic: The twelfth month opened on bingshen.

sentences.zh: 庚子，以東都留守韋夏卿為太子少保，以兵部尚書王紹為東都留守。

translations.literal: On gengzi Wei Xiaqing, eastern capital regent, was made Junior Tutor of the Heir; Wang Shao, Minister of War, was made eastern capital regent.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xiaqing and Wang Shao exchanged eastern capital posts on gengzi.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，改淳縣為清溪縣，姓淳於者改姓於。

translations.literal: On renyin Chun county was renamed Qingxi county; those surnamed Chunyu changed their surname to Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Chun county became Qingxi and the Chunyu clan changed their name on renyin.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，襄陽于頔加平章事。

translations.literal: On jiachen Yu Di of Xiangyang was made Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Di of Xiangyang entered the council on jiachen.

sentences.zh: 丙申，月犯畢。

translations.literal: On bingshen the moon trespassed upon Bi.
translations.idiomatic: The moon crossed the Bi asterism on bingshen.

sentences.zh: 己酉，以新除給事中、西川行軍司馬劉辟為成都尹、劍南西川節度使。

translations.literal: On jiyou the newly appointed Supervisor of Attendants and Sichuan campaign staff officer Liu Pi was made Governor of Chengdu and Sichuan military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Pi received Sichuan on jiyou — a fatal appointment.

sentences.zh: 歲星犯太微西垣。

translations.literal: The Year Star trespassed upon the western rampart of Supreme Palace Enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: Jupiter crossed the western wall of the Imperial Enclosure.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，金州復析漢陰縣置石泉縣。

translations.literal: On gengxu Jinzhou again split off Shiyin county to establish Shiquan county.
translations.idiomatic: Shiquan county was carved from Shiyin on gengxu.

sentences.zh: 壬子，以右諫議大夫韋丹為梓州刺史，充劍南東川節度使，以常州刺史路應為宣州刺史、宣歙池觀察使。

translations.literal: On renzi Right Remonstrator Wei Dan was made prefect of Zi and Sichuan eastern commissioner; Lu Ying, prefect of Changzhou, was made prefect of Xuan and Xuanchi-Chi observer.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Dan and Lu Ying took Sichuan and Huai-nan posts on renzi.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，以朝請大夫、守中書舍人、翰林學士、上柱國鄭絪為中書侍郎、同平章事、集賢殿學士。

translations.literal: On renxu Zheng Yin, Grand Master for Court Audience, acting Secretariat Drafter, Hanlin academician, and pillar of the state, was made Vice Director of the Secretariat, Grand Councillor, and Academician of the Hall for Assembling Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yin joined the council on renxu.

sentences.zh: 以考功郎中、知制誥李吉甫為中書舍人，以考功員外郎裴為考功郎中、知制誥，並充翰林學士。

translations.literal: Li Jifu, bureau director in the Ministry of Personnel and drafter of edicts, was made Secretariat Drafter; Pei, outer bureau director in the Ministry of Personnel, was made bureau director and drafter of edicts; both were also Hanlin academicians.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jifu, Pei, and others entered the Hanlin.

sentences.zh: 春正月丙寅朔，皇帝率群臣于興慶宮奉上太上皇號曰應乾聖壽太上皇。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, bingyin new moon — the Emperor led the ministers at Xingqing Palace to present to the Retired Emperor the title Responding to Heaven, Sagely Longevity Retired Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month Xianzong offered his father the full retired honorific at Xingqing.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，禦含元殿受朝賀。

translations.literal: On dingmao he took Hanyuan Hall to receive court congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: He received New Year felicitations at Hanyuan on dingmao.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，禦丹鳳樓，大赦天下，改元曰元和。

translations.literal: When the rites were complete, he took Danfeng Tower, proclaimed a great amnesty for the empire, and changed the era name to Yuanhe.
translations.idiomatic: From Danfeng he proclaimed amnesty and the Yuanhe era.

sentences.zh: 自正月二日昧爽已前，大辟罪已下，常赦不原者，鹹赦除之。

translations.literal: From before dawn on the second day of the first month, great execution and below, normally not pardoned by regular amnesties, were all pardoned and removed.
translations.idiomatic: Even capital crimes usually excluded from amnesty were forgiven.

sentences.zh: 辛未，以鄂嶽沔觀察使韓皋為鄂、嶽、蘄、安、黃等州節度使。

translations.literal: On xinwei Han Gao, E-Yue-Mian observer, was made military commissioner of E, Yue, Qi, An, and Huang.
translations.idiomatic: Han Gao received a broader Hubei command on xinwei.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，太子少保韋夏卿卒。

translations.literal: On dingchou Junior Tutor of the Heir Wei Xiaqing died.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xiaqing died on dingchou.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，以興元元從功臣、右神策護軍使副薛盈珍為右神策護軍中尉。

translations.literal: On xinsi Xue Yingzhen, meritorious follower from the Yuanhe restoration and vice protector of the Right Divine Strategy Army, was made lieutenant protector of the Right Divine Strategy Army.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Yingzhen became a Shence army eunuch commander on xinsi.

sentences.zh: 壬午，成德軍節度使、檢校司空王士真同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: On renwu Wang Shizhen, Chengde military commissioner and acting Master of Works, was made Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shizhen of Chengde entered the council on renwu.

sentences.zh: 癸未，詔以太上皇舊恙愆和，親侍藥膳，起今月十六日已後，權不聽政。

translations.literal: On guiwei an edict: because the Retired Emperor's old illness was out of harmony, personally attending with medicine and food — from the sixteenth of this month onward, he is provisionally not to hear government.
translations.idiomatic: The retired emperor's illness suspended audiences from the sixteenth on guiwei.

sentences.zh: 以左神策長武城防秋都知兵馬使高崇文檢校工部尚書，充神策行營節度使。

translations.literal: Gao Chongwen, Changwu city autumn-defense commander of the Left Divine Strategy Army, was made acting Minister of Works and Shence campaign military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Chongwen was appointed to crush Liu Pi in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 甲申，太上皇崩于興慶宮，遷殯於太極殿，發喪。

translations.literal: On jiashen the Retired Emperor died in Xingqing Palace; the coffin was moved to the Hall of Supreme Ultimate and mourning was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: Shunzong died again in the annals' Yuanhe frame — mourning began on jiashen.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，宰相杜祐攝塚宰，杜黃裳為禮儀使，右僕射伊慎大明宮留守，視事於尚書省。

translations.literal: On yiyou Grand Councillor Du You acted as chief mourner; Du Huangchang as ritual commissioner; Right Vice Director Yi Zhen as Daming Palace regent, conducting affairs at the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The funeral bureaucracy was organized on yiyou.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，復置斜谷路館驛。

translations.literal: On renchen the Xiegu road courier stations were restored.
translations.idiomatic: Xiegu postal stations reopened on renchen.

sentences.zh: 戊子，制：「劍南西川，疆界素定，籓鎮守備，各有區分。

translations.literal: On wuzi an order: "Southwestern Sichuan — borders long settled, frontier commands and garrisons each have divisions.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi an expedition edict opened:

sentences.zh: 頃因元臣薨謝，鄰籓不睦，劉辟乃因虛構隙，以忿結仇，遂勞王軍，兼害百姓。

translations.literal: Recently because a great minister died, neighboring commands were not at peace; Liu Pi then exploited the void to fabricate a rift, nursing wrath into enmity, and so tired the royal army and also harmed the people.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Pi had seized on Wei Gao's death to rebel and harm the people.

sentences.zh: 朕志存含垢，務欲安人，遣使諭宣，委之旄鉞。

translations.literal: My will stores tolerance for filth and seeks only to settle the people; I sent envoys to proclaim and instruct and entrusted him with the commander's banner.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had tried appeasement before force.

sentences.zh: 如聞道路擁塞，未息干戈，輕肆攻圍，擬圖吞併。

translations.literal: I hear roads are blocked and war has not ceased; he lightly dares sieges and plots annexation.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Pi still blocked roads and besieged cities.

sentences.zh: 為君之體，義在勝殘，命將興師，蓋非獲已。

translations.literal: The body of being a ruler — righteousness lies in overcoming cruelty; ordering generals and raising armies is surely not obtained willingly.
translations.idiomatic: War was a reluctant duty of rule.

sentences.zh: 宜令興元嚴礪、東川李康掎角應接，神策行營節度使高崇文、神策兵馬使李元奕率步騎之師，與東川、興元之師類會進討。

translations.literal: It is fitting to order Xingyuan Yan Li, eastern Sichuan Li Kang to coordinate pincers, Shence campaign commissioner Gao Chongwen and Shence army commander Li Yuanyi to lead infantry and cavalry, and with eastern Sichuan and Xingyuan armies jointly advance to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Li, Li Kang, Gao Chongwen, and Li Yuanyi were ordered to converge on Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 其糧料供餉，委度支使差官以聞。

translations.literal: Grain and supplies — commission the revenue commissioner to dispatch officials and report."
translations.idiomatic: Logistics were assigned to the fiscal office. Thus ended the edict.

sentences.zh: 」甲午，高崇文之師由斜谷路，李元奕之師由駱谷路，俱會於梓潼。

translations.literal: On jiawu Gao Chongwen's army by the Xiegu road and Li Yuanyi's army by the Luogu road both assembled at Zitong.
translations.idiomatic: The two columns met at Zitong on jiawu.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，群臣請聽政。

translations.literal: On xinmao the host of ministers asked that he hear government.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers petitioned him to resume rule on xinmao.

sentences.zh: 二月乙未朔，以度支郎中敬寬為山劍行營糧料使。

translations.literal: Second month, yiwei new moon — Jing Kuan, bureau director in the Ministry of Revenue, was made grain commissioner of the Shannan-Sichuan campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Kuan became campaign quartermaster in the second month.

sentences.zh: 嚴礪奏收劍州。

translations.literal: Yan Li memorialized recovery of Jianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Li reported taking Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，入朝奚王梅落可銀青光錄大夫、檢校司空，封饒樂郡王，放還蕃。

translations.literal: On yichou the visiting Xi king Meiluo was made Silver-Green Glory Grand Master, acting Master of Works, enfeoffed Prince of Raole, and sent back to Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: The Xi king Meiluo was honored and sent home on yichou.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，贈宣武軍節度使陸長源為右僕射，贈故吉州刺史姜公輔禮部尚書。

translations.literal: On guimao Lu Changyuan, Xuanwu military commissioner, was posthumously made Right Vice Director; the late Prefect of Ji Jiang Gongfu was posthumously made Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Changyuan and Jiang Gongfu were posthumously honored on guimao.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，以錢少，禁用銅器。

translations.literal: On jiachen because money was scarce, use of copper vessels was forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Copper utensils were banned to save coin on jiachen.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，以魏博田季安同平章事。

translations.literal: On guichou Tian Ji'an of Weibo was made Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Ji'an of Weibo entered the council on guichou.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，謂宰臣曰：「前代帝王，或怠於聽政，或躬決繁務，其道如何。

translations.literal: On wuxu he told the councillors: "Former dynasties' emperors — some were slack in hearing government, some personally decided complex affairs — what of their Ways?
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu he asked his ministers how an emperor should govern.

sentences.zh: 」杜黃裳對曰：「帝王之務，在於修己簡易，擇賢委任，宵旰以求民瘼，舍己從人以厚下，固不宜怠肆安逸。

translations.literal: "Du Huangchang replied: "An emperor's task lies in cultivating the self with simplicity, choosing the worthy and entrusting them, from dawn seeking the people's sores, setting aside the self to follow others to enrich those below — solidly he should not be slack, dissipated, or at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Du Huangchang urged diligence and delegation, not micromanagement.

sentences.zh: 然事有綱領小大，當務知其遠者大者；

translations.literal: Yet affairs have large and small outlines; one should strive to know the distant and the great;
translations.idiomatic: The ruler must grasp great ends, he said,

sentences.zh: 至如簿書訟獄，百吏能否，本非人主所自任也。

translations.literal: as for ledgers, lawsuits, and the hundred clerks' competence — these are fundamentally not what the human ruler personally bears.
translations.idiomatic: not clerks' paperwork or petty suits.

sentences.zh: 昔秦始皇自程決事。

translations.literal: Formerly Qin Shihuang personally judged decisions.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Shihuang judged cases himself

sentences.zh: 見嗤前代；

translations.literal: and was mocked by former ages;
translations.idiomatic: and was mocked by history;

sentences.zh: 諸葛亮王霸之佐，二十罰以上皆自省之，亦為敵國所誚，知不久堪；

translations.literal: Zhuge Liang, aide to kingly hegemony — above twenty lashes he all examined himself — and was also ridiculed by the enemy state, known not long to endure;
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang's reviewing every harsh punishment was scorned by rivals;

sentences.zh: 魏明帝欲省尚書擬事，陳矯言其不可；

translations.literal: Wei Mingdi wished to reduce the Secretariat's drafting of affairs — Chen Qiao said it could not be done;
translations.idiomatic: Wei Mingdi's plan to bypass the Secretariat was rebuked;

sentences.zh: 隋文帝日旰聽政，令衛士傳餐，文皇帝亦笑其煩察。

translations.literal: Sui Wendi at sundown heard government and ordered guards to pass meals — Emperor Wen also laughed at his finicky scrutiny.
translations.idiomatic: even Sui Wendi's dinner-table audiences were laughed at as excessive.

sentences.zh: 為人主之體固不可代下司職，但擇人委任，責其成效，賞罰必信，誰不盡心。

translations.literal: The body of being human ruler solidly cannot replace subordinates' offices; only choose men and entrust, demand their results, rewards and punishments must be trusted — who will not give their utmost?
translations.idiomatic: A sage-king trusts ministers, rewards faithfully, and does not do their work.

sentences.zh: 《傳》稱帝舜之德曰：'夫何為哉？

translations.literal: The Tradition says of Emperor Shun's virtue: 'What does he do?
translations.idiomatic: Du Huangchang quoted the Analects on Shun:

sentences.zh: 恭己南面而已！

translations.literal: Reverently facing south — that is all!'
translations.idiomatic: 'He merely faces south with reverence!'

sentences.zh: '誠以能舉十六相，去四凶也。

translations.literal: Truly because he could raise the sixteen ministers and remove the four villains.
translations.idiomatic: Shun ruled by appointing the worthy and banishing the wicked.

sentences.zh: 豈與勞神疲體自任耳目之主同年而語哉！

translations.literal: How can he be spoken of in the same year as a lord who wearies spirit and body and personally bears eyes and ears!
translations.idiomatic: Such a ruler is no model for a tired micromanager.

sentences.zh: 但人主常勢。

translations.literal: Yet the human ruler's constant tendency —
translations.idiomatic: Yet rulers, he added,

sentences.zh: 患在不能推誠，人臣之弊，患在不能自竭。

translations.literal: the worry is inability to extend sincerity; ministers' flaw is inability to exhaust themselves.
translations.idiomatic: fail from distrust; ministers fail from withholding effort.

sentences.zh: 由是上疑下詐，禮貌或虧，欲求致理，自然難致。

translations.literal: Hence above suspects and below deceives; ritual courtesy may be damaged — wishing to attain order, naturally it is hard to attain.
translations.idiomatic: Suspicion breeds fraud and makes good order impossible.

sentences.zh: 苟無此弊，何患不至於理。

translations.literal: If without these flaws, what worry is there of not reaching order?
translations.idiomatic: Without that mutual flaw, order would follow.

sentences.zh: '上稱善久之。

translations.literal: 'The Emperor praised it long.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him at length.

sentences.zh: 以京兆尹李鄘為尚書右丞，以金吾大將軍鄭雲逵為京兆尹。

translations.literal: Li Yong, Metropolitan Governor, was made Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; Grand General of the Golden Guard Zheng Yunkui was made Metropolitan Governor.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yong and Zheng Yunkui exchanged capital posts.

sentences.zh: 三月乙丑朔。

translations.literal: Third month, yichou new moon.
translations.idiomatic: The third month opened on yichou.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，詔常參官寒食拜墓，在畿內聽假日往還，他州府奏取進止。

translations.literal: On wuchen an edict: regular-attendance officials may visit graves at Cold Food — within the capital circuit they are permitted holiday travel back and forth; other prefectures and circuits memorialized for decision.
translations.idiomatic: Cold Food grave visits were regulated for capital officials on wuchen.

sentences.zh: 辛未，御史中丞武元衡奏：「中書門下御史台五品已上官、尚書省四品已上、諸司正三品已上、從三品職事官、東都留守、轉運鹽鐵節度觀察使、團練防禦招討經略等使、河南尹、同華州刺史、諸衛將軍三品已上官除授，皆入合謝，其餘官許于宣政南班拜訖便退。

translations.literal: On xinwei Vice Censor-in-Chief Wu Yuanheng memorialized: "Officials of the Secretariat-Chancellery and Censorate of fifth rank and above, the Department of State Affairs of fourth rank and above, all regular third rank and above, acting third rank and above, eastern capital regent, transport and salt commissioners, military observation commissioners, defense and campaign commissioners, Governor of Henan, Governors of Tong and Hua, generals of the guards of third rank and above — on appointment all enter the hall to give thanks; other officials are permitted to bow at the southern court of Xuanzheng and withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yuanheng defined which appointees must attend formal thanksgiving audiences.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「如此例中有加使及職掌並准此。

translations.literal: "An edict said: "Where this precedent includes added commissioners and duties, all follow this.
translations.idiomatic: The throne extended the rule to concurrent commissioners. Thus ended the edict.

sentences.zh: 」又「兵部、吏部、禮部貢院官員，每舉選限內，有十月至二月不奉朝參。

translations.literal: "Also: "Personnel of the War, Personnel, and Rites examination bureaus — within each selection limit, from the tenth month to the second month do not attend court.
translations.idiomatic: Examination officials had long claimed exemption from winter audiences;

sentences.zh: 若稱事繁，則中書門下、御史台、度支、京兆府公事至重，朝謁如常。

translations.literal: If they claim affairs are numerous, then the Secretariat-Chancellery, Censorate, revenue office, and metropolitan government have affairs to the utmost — court attendance as usual.
translations.idiomatic: but the edict noted heavier offices never skipped court.

sentences.zh: 況旬節已賜歸休，又許分日，一月之內，才奉十日朝參，甚暑甚寒，又蒙矜放。

translations.literal: Moreover seasonal holidays already grant return rest, and divided days are also permitted — within one month they attend court only ten days; in great heat and great cold they are also shown compassion.
translations.idiomatic: They already had holidays and half-days off, it argued.

sentences.zh: 臣求故實，以為王顏任中丞日嘗論其事，舉對甚詳。

translations.literal: Your subject seeks former precedent and holds that when Wang Yan held the censorate he once discussed this matter and answered in great detail.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yuanheng cited Wang Yan's earlier precedent.

sentences.zh: 伏請准貞元十二年四月二十七日敕，永為常式。

translations.literal: I humbly ask that the edict of Zhenyuan 12, fourth month, twenty-seventh day, be followed forever as constant form."
translations.idiomatic: He asked to restore the Zhenyuan 12 rule permanently.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: "It was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The throne agreed.

sentences.zh: 丙子，嚴礪收梓州。

translations.literal: On bingzi Yan Li recovered Zizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Li took Zizhou on bingzi.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，制削奪劉辟在身官爵。

translations.literal: On dingchou an order stripped Liu Pi of all offices held in life.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Pi was stripped of rank on dingchou.

sentences.zh: 先是韓全義入朝，令其甥楊惠琳知留後，俄有詔除李演為節度，代全義。

translations.literal: Earlier Han Quanyi entered court; he ordered his nephew Yang Huilin to act as regent; soon an edict appointed Li Yan military commissioner in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: Han Quanyi's nephew Yang Huilin had held the command until Li Yan was appointed.

sentences.zh: 演赴任，惠琳據城叛，詔發河東、天德兵誅之。

translations.literal: Yan went to his post; Huilin held the city in rebellion; an edict sent Hedong and Tiande troops to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Huilin rebelled when Li Yan arrived; imperial troops were sent.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，夏州兵馬使張承金斬惠琳，傳首以獻。

translations.literal: On xinsi Xiazhou army commander Zhang Chengjin beheaded Huilin and sent the head as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chengjin killed Huilin and presented his head on xinsi.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，大行太上皇德妃董氏卒。

translations.literal: On renchen the late Retired Emperor's Virtuous Consort Lady Dong died.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Dong, Shunzong's consort, died on renchen.

sentences.zh: 以右神策行營節度高崇文檢校兵部尚書、梓州刺史、劍南東川節度。

translations.literal: Gao Chongwen, Shence campaign commissioner, was made acting Minister of War, prefect of Zi, and eastern Sichuan military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Chongwen received eastern Sichuan command.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，以安南經略副使張舟為安南都護、本管經略使。

translations.literal: On wuxu Zhang Zhou, Annan pacification vice commissioner, was made Protector-General of Annan and circuit commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhou took Annan on wuxu.

sentences.zh: 己亥，以前劍南東川節度使韋丹為晉絳觀察使。

translations.literal: On jihai former eastern Sichuan military commissioner Wei Dan was made Jin-He observer.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Dan went to the Jin-He circuit on jihai.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，以前安南經略使趙昌為廣州刺史、嶺南節度使。

translations.literal: On renyin former Annan military commissioner Zhao Chang was made prefect of Guang and Lingnan military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Chang became Lingnan commissioner on renyin.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，前嶺南節度使徐申卒。

translations.literal: On guimao former Lingnan military commissioner Xu Shen died.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shen died on guimao.

sentences.zh: 丙午，命宰臣監試製舉人于尚書省，以制舉人先朝所征，不欲親試也。

translations.literal: On bingwu the councillors were ordered to supervise examination of decree-examination candidates at the Department of State Affairs — because decree candidates were summoned by the former dynasty and he did not wish to examine personally.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers supervised the decree exam rather than the emperor on bingwu.

sentences.zh: 丁未，以檢校司空、平章事杜祐為司徒，所司備禮冊拜，平章事如故；

translations.literal: On dingwei Du You, acting Master of Works and Grand Councillor, was made Minister of Education; the relevant offices prepared rites for enfeoffment and bowing; Grand Councillor as before;
translations.idiomatic: Du You became Minister of Education on dingwei while keeping the council;

sentences.zh: 罷領度支、鹽鐵、轉運等使，從其讓也，仍以兵部侍即李巽代領其任。

translations.literal: he ceased leading revenue, salt, iron, and transport commissions — following his declination — and Vice Minister of War Li Xun was still made to lead those duties.
translations.idiomatic: he yielded fiscal posts to Li Xun.

sentences.zh: 戊申，以隴右經略使、秦州經略使、秦州刺史劉澭為保義軍節度使。

translations.literal: On wushen Liu Zhan, Longyou pacification commissioner, Qinzhou pacification commissioner, and prefect of Qin, was made Baoyi army military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhan took the Baoyi command on wushen.

sentences.zh: 賑浙東米十萬石。

translations.literal: Zhedong was given 100,000 piculs of relief grain.
translations.idiomatic: Zhedong received famine relief grain.

sentences.zh: 己未，武元衡奏，常參官兼御史大夫、中丞者，准檢校省官例，立在本品同類之上。

translations.literal: On jiwei Wu Yuanheng memorialized: regular-attendance officials who are concurrent Censor-in-Chief or vice censor — follow the precedent for acting provincial officials, standing above others of the same original rank.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yuanheng fixed precedence for censor-concurrents on jiwei.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，邵王約薨。

translations.literal: On renxu Prince of Shao Yue died.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yue of Shao died on renxu.

sentences.zh: 武元衡奏：「正衙待制官，本置此官以備問。

translations.literal: Wu Yuanheng memorialized: "Regular-attendance awaiting-order officials — originally this office was established to prepare for questioning.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yuanheng revived the awaiting-order institution:

sentences.zh: 比來正衙多不奏事。

translations.literal: Recently at regular court many do not present business.
translations.idiomatic: recently none had spoken at court.

sentences.zh: 自今後請以尚書省六品以上職事官、東宮師傅賓詹、王傅等，每坐日令兩人待制，退朝，詔于延英候對。

translations.literal: From now on let officials of the Department of State Affairs of sixth rank and above with substantive posts, eastern palace tutors, companions, and princes' tutors — each court day two await order; after court, order them to wait at Yanying for audience."
translations.idiomatic: Two senior officials per day would wait at Yanying to advise the emperor.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: "It was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The throne agreed.

sentences.zh: 五月甲子朔。

translations.literal: Fifth month, jiazi new moon.
translations.idiomatic: The fifth month opened on jiazi.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，京兆尹鄭雲逵卒。

translations.literal: On dingmao Metropolitan Governor Zheng Yunkui died.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yunkui died on dingmao.

sentences.zh: 辛未，以兵部侍郎韋武為京兆尹兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: On xinwei Wei Wu, Vice Minister of War, was made Metropolitan Governor and concurrent Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Wu became capital intendant on xinwei.

sentences.zh: 壬申，貶劍南東川節度使李康為雷州司馬。

translations.literal: On renshen eastern Sichuan military commissioner Li Kang was demoted to staff officer of Lei.
translations.idiomatic: Li Kang was exiled to Lei on renshen.

sentences.zh: 陳、許、蔡等州旱。

translations.literal: Chen, Xu, Cai, and other prefectures suffered drought.
translations.idiomatic: Central plains drought continued.

sentences.zh: 以橫海軍留後程執恭橫海軍節度使。

translations.literal: Zhigong, regent of the Transocean Army, was made Transocean military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Zhigong received full command of the Transocean army.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，左丞、同平章事鄭余慶為太子賓客，罷知政事。

translations.literal: On gengchen Left Vice Director and Grand Councillor Zheng Yuqing was made Junior Mentor to the Heir and ceased handling administration.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yuqing left the council for the heir's tutorate on gengchen.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，冊太上皇后王氏為皇太后。

translations.literal: On xinmao Retired Empress Lady Wang was enfeoffed Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wang became empress dowager on xinmao.

sentences.zh: 六月癸己朔，以冊太后禮畢，赦天下系囚，死罪降從流，流以下遞減一等。

translations.literal: Sixth month, guisi new moon — because the empress dowager's investiture rites were complete, capital prisoners were pardoned — death reduced to exile, exile and below reduced one grade in succession.
translations.idiomatic: A partial amnesty followed the dowager's rites on guisi.

sentences.zh: 文武內外官加母邑號，太后諸親，量與優給。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials within and without were given posthumous titles on their mothers; the dowager's kin were measured out favorable grants.
translations.idiomatic: Officials' mothers received honors and the dowager's kin gifts.

sentences.zh: 丙申，冊德宗充容武氏為崇陵德妃。

translations.literal: On bingshen Lady Wu, Full Consort of Dezong, was enfeoffed Chongling Virtuous Consort.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wu was enfeoffed consort of Chongling on bingshen.

sentences.zh: 大風折樹。

translations.literal: Great wind broke trees.
translations.idiomatic: A gale uprooted trees.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，高崇文破賊萬人于鹿頭關。

translations.literal: On dingyou Gao Chongwen broke ten thousand bandits at Lutou Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Chongwen routed Liu Pi's army at Lutou Pass on dingyou.

sentences.zh: 加幽州劉濟侍中，淄青李師古檢校司徒。

translations.literal: Liu Ji of Youzhou was made Palace Attendant; Li Shigu of Ziqing was made acting Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ji and Li Shigu received honorary titles.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，高崇文收漢州。

translations.literal: On guimao Gao Chongwen recovered Hanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hanzhou fell to Gao Chongwen on guimao.

sentences.zh: 閏六月壬子朔，淄青李師古卒。

translations.literal: Intercalary sixth month, renzi new moon — Li Shigu of Ziqing died.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shigu of Shandong died in the intercalary sixth month.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，以秘書監董叔經為京兆尹。

translations.literal: On wuchen Director of the Palace Library Dong Shujing was made Metropolitan Governor.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Shujing became capital intendant on wuchen.

sentences.zh: 壬午，諫議大夫去左、右字，只置四員。

translations.literal: On renwu the Remonstrators lost the Left and Right designations; only four posts were kept.
translations.idiomatic: The remonstrance was reduced to four posts on renwu.

sentences.zh: 以前司封員外郎韋況為諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Former outer bureau director in the Ministry of Personnel Wei Kuang was made Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Kuang became remonstrator.
